correctness.rationale: Exact Gaussian differentiation gives J=delta I+a u^T. The symmetric rank-two eigenvalues are (u·a ± ||u||||a||)/2; g''(0)=0 makes the true objective locally isotropic, yielding the positive finite-step coefficient -h v^T Jv + (h^2/2)||Jv||^2 for every fixed h>0 when delta<delta_*. For the explicit globally smooth strongly convex example, c1=1/(2sqrt(2)), c2=100/101^(3/2), and the rational witness has v^T Jv<0 by exact elementary inequalities. Standalone standard-library verifier passed 63 independent differentiation, Gaussian-integration, matrix, and finite-step checks; no finite check is substituted for proof.

value.rationale: Fixed-step derivative-free optimization routinely uses a smoothed surrogate direction; whether smooth strong convexity safeguards true objective descent is a natural algorithmic question. The result gives a sharp general ridge-local criterion and an explicit exact-integral counterexample valid against every positive fixed stepsize arbitrarily close to the unique minimizer. It separates intrinsic DGS direction geometry from quadrature noise, while making no global divergence or practical line-search claim.
